Hon'ble Mrs. Sadhna Rani (Thakur),J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants and perused the record.

By moving this application prayer is made to quash the charge sheet dated 18.11.2020, cognizance order dated 18.01.2021 and the entire proceedings of Case No. 218 of 2021 (state Vs. Deepak Singh and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 0954 of 2018, under sections 188, 288, 420 IPC and Section 7 of Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1932, Police Station Bisrakh, District Gautam Budh Nagar.

It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicants that the on the same cause of action FIR dated 18.01.2021 was filed by the same first informant against 19 persons that they were raising constructions without getting any map passed and getting any permission from the authority,
wherein final report was filed on 03.02.2019.

Before filing this final report, on 16.10.2018 against same 19 persons separate 19 FIRs were filed by the same first informant and against both the FIRs the applicants approached this court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. No offence

sentences.text: Moreover, the summoning order 18.01.2021 has been filed on the prescribed proforma just by filling the blanks, which shows the non application of judicial mind in passing the order.
Hence, prayer is made accordingly.
If we go through the impugned order dated 18.01.2021 it is passed on the printed proforma just by filling the blanks.

So far as the argument that the cognizance order has been passed on a printed proforma is concerned, although it has been held by this Court in the case of Megh Nath Gupta & another Vs.
State of U.P. and another, 2008 (62) ACC 826 that the Magistrate is not required to pass detailed reasoned order at the time of taking cognizance on the charge-sheet, but it does not mean that order of taking cognizance can be passed by filling up the blanks on printed proforma.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At the time of passing any judicial order including the order taking cognizance on the charge-sheet, the court is required to apply its judicial mind and even the order of taking cognizance cannot be passed in mechanical manner.

Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Harischandra Prasad Mani and others Vs.
State of Jharkhand and another (2007) 15 Supreme Court Cases 494, Fakhruddin Ahmad Vs. State of Uttaranchal and another (2008) 17 Supreme Court Cases 157 and Ankit Vs. State of U.P. and others, U.P. Criminal Report 2009 (3) 427 has established that if the order on printed proforma is passed it establishes that the Magistrate concerned has not applied his mind to the evidence on record in order to take cognizance of the offence concerned.

sentences.text: In the present case also the cognizance order has been passed by the Magistrate concerned on a printed proforma just by filling up the blanks in the order, which clearly shows that the Magistrate concerned did not apply his judicial mind and did not go through the material collected by the Investigating Officer against the applicants in the case.
The result is that the order impugned dated 18.01.2021, which has been passed by filling the blanks on the printed proforma is illegal, incorrect and improper, which cannot be sustained.
Hence, the order dated 18.01.2021 is liable to be quashed.
Without going into the merits of the case cognizance/summoning order dated 18.01.2021 is hereby quashed.
The trial court is directed to pass a fresh order regarding cognizance within one month as per law.
The application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is disposed of.
A copy of this order be sent to the court concerned.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
At the time of passing any judicial order including the order taking cognizance on the charge-sheet, the court is required to apply its judicial mind and even the order of taking cognizance cannot be passed in mechanical manner.
Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Harischandra Prasad Mani and others Vs.
State of Jharkhand and another (2007) 15 Supreme Court Cases 494, Fakhruddin Ahmad Vs. State of Uttaranchal and another (2008) 17 Supreme Court Cases 157 and Ankit Vs. State of U.P. and others, U.P. Criminal Report 2009 (3) 427 has established that if the order on printed proforma is passed it establishes that the Magistrate concerned has not applied his mind to the evidence on record in order to take cognizance of the offence concerned.
In the present case also the cognizance order has been passed by the Magistrate concerned on a printed proforma just by filling up the blanks in the order, which clearly shows that the Magistrate concerned did not apply his judicial mind and did not go through the material collected by the Investigating Officer against the applicants in the case.
